entries.long:
Deterministic Markdown vault graph tools

USAGE
    norn [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

COMMANDS
    find              Find documents in the vault — full-text + metadata filters with sort/limit/paging
    count             Count documents in the vault — grouped or total — with the find filter surface
    describe          Describe the vault: structure counts, the declared config with --schema, a contents-summary with --data
    get               Get one or more documents — frontmatter, headings, outgoing/incoming/unresolved links
    set               Update one document — schema-aware frontmatter mutation + wholesale body replacement
    edit              Edit one document's body — atomic content-anchored partial edits
    new               Create a new document — schema-aware frontmatter pre-fill from path rules
    init              Scaffold .norn/config.yaml
    move              Move/rename a document with cascading backlink rewrites
    delete            Delete a document, optionally redirecting incoming links to an alternate target
    apply             Apply a MigrationPlan — execute move, delete, rewrite, and frontmatter ops from a plan file
    repair            Surface deterministic-repair findings; --plan emits a MigrationPlan
    rewrite-wikilink  Rewrite all occurrences of a wikilink target across the vault (body + frontmatter)
    validate          Validate vault graph facts and configured frontmatter rules
    completions       Shell completion installation and script emission
    cache             Manage the SQLite-backed vault graph cache
    config            Manage the per-vault `.norn/config.yaml`
    self-update       Update norn to the latest GitHub release
    mcp               Run norn as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) stdio server over the vault at --cwd
    serve             Run the warm host daemon: serves MCP for any vault on this host over a Unix socket
    service           Supervise the warm `norn serve` daemon under launchd (macOS): install/uninstall/start/stop/restart/status
    audit             Read the vault mutation audit trail (the append-only event stream): recent mutations with status / target / trace, filterable
    vault             Manage the vault registry — register a vault to unlock durable artifacts (cache, event stream, logs)

EXAMPLES
    norn find --eq type:note --limit 5
        # 5 notes by default sort

    norn validate --format json
        # machine-readable validation findings

    norn repair --plan --out plan.json
        # generate a MigrationPlan

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

Documentation: https://github.com/dbtlr/norn

entries.long:
Apply a MigrationPlan — execute move, delete, rewrite, and frontmatter ops from a plan file

USAGE
    norn apply [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS
    <PLAN>
        Path to MigrationPlan file (YAML or JSON). Use `-` for stdin

OPTIONS
        --input-format <INPUT_FORMAT>
        Input plan format. Auto-detected by extension (.yaml/.yml → YAML, else JSON). Required for stdin (`-`) when the plan is YAML
        Possible values: json, yaml

    -p, --parents
        Auto-create missing parent directories for create_document ops (mkdir -p style). Directories are created only for ops that proceed
        Possible values: true, false

        --out <OUT>
        Write the JSON apply report to this file instead of stdout

        --yes
        Apply the change without an interactive confirm prompt
        Possible values: true, false

        --dry-run
        Preview the change without writing
        Possible values: true, false

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format; `json` emits the mutation-report envelope
        Possible values: records, json

HOW APPLY WRITES
    Apply walks the MigrationPlan in this order:

    1. Load the plan JSON and verify its schema version.
    2. Confirm the plan's recorded vault root matches the effective cwd.
    3. Re-read each source document and verify its hash matches what the plan recorded; abort if any file changed since plan time.
    4. Verify each `expected_old_value` matches the current field value; abort on mismatch.
    5. Write the new frontmatter, preserving the Markdown body.
    6. Re-run validate when `--verify` is set.

    Pass `--dry-run` to walk steps 1–4 without writing.

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

Documentation: https://github.com/dbtlr/norn

entries.long:
Read the vault mutation audit trail (the append-only event stream): recent mutations with status / target / trace, filterable

USAGE
    norn audit [OPTIONS]

FILTERS
        --trace <ID>
        Only events from this invocation trace id (one mutation command)

        --status <STATUS>
        Only per-action events with this status. Excludes lifecycle/planned events (which have no status)
        Possible values: applied, skipped, failed

        --target <PATH>
        Only events touching this vault-relative path (matches a move's source or destination)

        --since <WHEN>
        Lower time bound. `YYYY-MM-DD` (start of UTC day) or full RFC-3339

        --until <WHEN>
        Upper time bound. `YYYY-MM-DD` (end of UTC day) or full RFC-3339

SORT AND PAGING
        --limit <N>
        Maximum number of events to return, newest-first

OUTPUT
        --raw
        Emit the stored OTEL event objects verbatim instead of the flattened projection. Affects `--format json` only (ignored by `records`)
        Possible values: true, false

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format. Default records (vertical key-value block per event)
        Possible values: records, json

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

Edit one document's body — atomic content-anchored partial edits

Edit one document's body with atomic, content-anchored partial edits.

The ops are an ordered array applied all-or-nothing, each against the result of the prior. Any anchor that fails to match refuses the whole batch (exit 2) and writes nothing — a `str_replace` whose `old` is missing, or matches more than once without `--replace-all`; a heading that names two sections, which refuses as ambiguous rather than guessing. Replace a whole body, or change frontmatter, with `norn set` instead.

USAGE
    norn edit [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS
    <DOC>
        The doc to edit. Path, stem, or wikilink-shaped (with or without [[]])

OPTIONS
        --edits-json <JSON>
        The edits as a JSON array of ops (e.g. `[{"op":"str_replace","old":"a","new":"b"}]`). Mutually exclusive with stdin; if omitted, the array is read from stdin

        --str-replace <OLD>
        Sugar: `str_replace` — the OLD anchor. Payload: `--new` (alias `--content`)

        --replace-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `replace_section` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --append-to-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `append_to_section` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --delete-section <HEADING>
        Sugar: `delete_section` — the HEADING anchor. No payload

        --insert-before-heading <HEADING>
        Sugar: `insert_before_heading` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        --insert-after-heading <HEADING>
        Sugar: `insert_after_heading` — the HEADING anchor. Payload: `--content`

        Payload for `--str-replace` (the replacement text; JSON field `new`)

        --content <BODY>
        Payload for the section ops (JSON field `content`); also an alias for `--new` on `--str-replace`

        Possible values: true, false

SORT AND PAGING
        --sort <FIELD>
        Sort by field (frontmatter key, `path`, or `stem`). Ascending by default

        --desc
        Sort descending (only meaningful with --sort)
        Possible values: true, false

        --limit <N>
        Maximum number of records to return. `find` defaults to 10; `get` returns every named target

        --no-limit
        Return all records; no limit. Competes with `--limit`; the last of the two given wins

Get one or more documents — frontmatter, headings, outgoing/incoming/unresolved links

Get one or more documents in detail.

Each target may be a vault-relative path, a unique case-insensitive document stem, or a wikilink-shaped string (with or without brackets, with or without anchor / block-ref / pipe-alias suffix). Ambiguous targets emit one record per resolved candidate. --all-cols adds the full structured dump (incl. body); --col narrows the default field set. Supports --sort/--limit/--starts-at over the named targets.

USAGE
    norn get [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS
    <DOC>
        One or more doc targets. Each accepts path, stem, or wikilink-shaped input (with or without [[]]). Anchor / block-ref / pipe-alias suffixes are stripped before resolution

SORT AND PAGING
        --sort <FIELD>
        Sort by field (frontmatter key, `path`, or `stem`). Ascending by default

        --desc
        Sort descending (only meaningful with --sort)
        Possible values: true, false

        --limit <N>
        Maximum number of records to return. `find` defaults to 10; `get` returns every named target

        --no-limit
        Return all records; no limit. Competes with `--limit`; the last of the two given wins
        Possible values: true, false

        --starts-at <N>
        Zero-indexed starting offset for paging. Default 0

OUTPUT
        --all-cols
        Emit the full structured dump: every frontmatter field plus every cache-served facet (`.headings`, the three link sets, `.body`). Competes with `--col` over the projection; the last of the two given wins
        Possible values: true, false

        --col <COL1,COL2,...>
        Comma-separated columns to include. Bare names select frontmatter fields (e.g. `status,title`), exactly like `norn find`. Structural facets are dot-prefixed: `.path`, `.stem`, `.frontmatter` (the whole block), `.headings`, `.outgoing_links`, `.unresolved_links`, `.incoming_links`, `.body`, `.document_hash` (the content hash `edit --expected-hash` wants; opt-in only — never in `--all-cols`). Without --col, frontmatter + headings + links are emitted (body only with --all-cols or `--col .body`)

        --section <HEADING>
        Named section to read, by exact heading text. Repeatable — pass once per section (`--section "Task Description" --section "Annotations"`). Each occurrence is one whole heading string, so a heading that itself contains a comma (`--section "Risks, Open Questions"`) is addressable verbatim — the same way `edit` takes a heading as one whole string. Resolved with the same boundary and failure semantics as `edit --append-to-section` / `--replace-section` (heading line through the next same-or-higher heading, or EOF) — a section read mirrors a section write. Orthogonal to `--col`/`--all-cols`; combine freely. A heading missing or ambiguous in a given document warns on stderr and is omitted from that document's `sections` (siblings and other documents are unaffected); if none of the requested headings resolve for a document, that is a hard failure (nonzero exit) for that target, mirroring how `get` already treats a target that fails to resolve at all. Ignored (with a warning) by `--format paths`/`markdown`, like `--col`

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format. Default records; markdown returns one exact source file
        Possible values: records, paths, json, jsonl, markdown

        --no-pager
        Skip the pager even when stdout is a TTY (NRN-454). `get` renders whole documents — the strongest long-form case — so it pages its `records` and `markdown` output exactly like `find` pages its `records` output
        Possible values: true, false

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)
        --verbose           Include full diagnostic detail in output
        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

entries.long:
Surface deterministic-repair findings; --plan emits a MigrationPlan

USAGE
    norn repair [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS
        --plan
        Generate a MigrationPlan from current findings (read-only). Without this flag, `norn repair` prints a findings summary instead
        Possible values: true, false

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format. Bare repair: `records` summary or `json` report envelope. --plan: records/json/paths (default: records on TTY, json when piped). `paths` requires --plan
        Possible values: records, json, paths

        --out <OUT>
        Write the JSON MigrationPlan artifact to this path instead of stdout (--plan only)

        --confidence <CONFIDENCE>
        Filter closest-match proposals by confidence band. Default: emit all bands. `high` drops Medium proposals (and their footnotes)
        Possible values: high

        --skip-reason <PATTERN>
        Filter skipped findings by reason code; glob patterns accepted (repeatable)

TRIAGE FILTERS
        --code <CODE>
        Filter findings by code. Comma-separated values match any listed code

        --severity <SEVERITY>
        Filter findings by severity

        --field <FIELD>
        Filter findings by frontmatter field

        --rule <RULE>
        Filter findings by validate rule name

        --path <PATH>
        Filter findings by vault-relative path glob using config glob semantics

        --target <TARGET>
        Filter link findings by link target

        --reason <REASON>
        Filter link findings by unresolved reason

EXAMPLES
    norn repair
        # summarize repairable findings; no writes

    norn repair --plan --out plan.json
        # write a MigrationPlan to file

    norn repair --plan --format json | norn apply -
        # generate a plan and apply it through apply

    norn repair --plan --format paths
        # affected paths only; pipe to xargs

    norn repair --plan --skip-reason ambiguous-target
        # show only ambiguous-target skips

    norn repair --plan --severity error
        # plan only error-level findings

THE PLAN/APPLY BOUNDARY
    Repair runs in two halves. `norn repair --plan` reads validate findings and emits a MigrationPlan JSON artifact describing every change it would make. Planning never writes to vault documents. `norn apply` consumes that artifact and writes the changes; preconditions are checked before any file is touched.

    Planning classifies each finding as supported or skipped. Supported findings produce a typed operation in the plan's `operations` list — its `kind` (e.g. `set_frontmatter`) plus a `fields` object carrying the path, the field, the new value, and the source document's hash recorded at plan time. Skipped findings carry a reason code (stable kebab-case string): `missing-default`, `link-decision-needed`, `no-rule-matched`, `graph-diagnostic`, `ambiguous-target`, `missing-hash`, or `precondition-failed`. Filter skipped findings with `--skip-reason <PATTERN>`; glob patterns accepted.

    A plan operation:

    {
      "kind": "set_frontmatter",
      "fields": {
        "path": "notes/welcome.md",
        "field": "kind",
        "new_value": "note",
        "document_hash": "a3f2…"
      }
    }

    A skipped finding records the reason (the `reason` value is the kebab-case skip-reason code; `finding_code` is the underlying validate code):

    {
      "finding_code": "link-ambiguous",
      "path": "drafts/x.md",
      "reason": "ambiguous-target"
    }

    The summary's `skipped` section uses a `by_reason` map: `{ "ambiguous-target": 3, "no-rule-matched": 12 }`. Zero-count buckets are omitted.

    `--plan` output formats: `--format records` (human summary, TTY default), `--format json` (full MigrationPlan envelope, pipe default), `--format paths` (one affected path per line, deduplicated). Bare `norn repair` (no `--plan`) has its own, narrower `--format`: `records` prints the findings summary as prose (the default) and `json` emits that same summary as a JSON envelope — `findings_total`, `total_docs`, the sorted `findings_by_code` tally, and the planner's `operations`/`skipped` counts — never the MigrationPlan; `paths` has no defined bare projection and requires `--plan`.

    The plan captures a vault snapshot. Each change records the document's hash at plan time; apply refuses to write if that hash has changed. Re-run `--plan` after editing files between plan and apply.

    Triage filters here are the same as on `validate` — pass `--severity error` to plan only error-level findings. Filters that excluded a finding from validate also exclude it from plan.

GLOBAL OPTIONS
    -C, --cwd <CWD>         Run as if norn started in this directory (default: $NORN_ROOT, else the current directory)

        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

entries.long:
Update one document — schema-aware frontmatter mutation + wholesale body replacement

USAGE
    norn set [OPTIONS]

ARGUMENTS
    <DOC>
        The doc to mutate. Path, stem, or wikilink-shaped (with or without [[]])

    <KEY=VALUE>
        Trailing `KEY=VALUE` positionals — sugar for `--field KEY=VALUE` (ADR 0010). Identical semantics: same schema coercion, same repeat-accumulates-to-array. Every positional AFTER DOC must contain a `:` or `=` separator or it is a hard error; the first positional is always DOC (a doc literally named `a=b.md` is still addressed as DOC)

OPTIONS
        --field <KEY=VALUE>
        Set a frontmatter field. Repeatable; multiple instances of the same key accumulate into an array. KEY=VALUE

        --field-json <KEY=JSON>
        Set a frontmatter field with a JSON-parsed value. Escape hatch for structured values (arrays, nested objects, explicit null). KEY=JSON

        --push <KEY=VALUE>
        Append a value to a list-typed frontmatter field. Creates a single-element array if the key doesn't exist. KEY=VALUE

        --pop <KEY=VALUE>
        Remove a value from a list-typed frontmatter field. Silent no-op if value not present. KEY=VALUE

        --remove <KEY>
        Remove a frontmatter key entirely. Silent no-op if key not present

        --body-from-stdin
        Read new body content from stdin (wholesale body replacement)
        Possible values: true, false

        --force
        Bypass schema enforcement (type validation + required-field protection)
        Possible values: true, false

        --yes
        Apply the change without an interactive confirm prompt
        Possible values: true, false

        --dry-run
        Preview the change without writing
        Possible values: true, false

        --format <FORMAT>
        Output format; `json` emits the mutation-report envelope
        Possible values: records, json

EXAMPLES
    norn set notes/project.md --field status=active --yes
        # set the `status` field to `active`; skip confirm

    norn set notes/project.md --push aliases=new-alias --yes
        # append a value to an array-typed frontmatter field

    norn set notes/project.md --pop aliases=old-name --yes
        # drop a value from an array; silent if absent

    norn set notes/project.md --remove priority --yes
        # remove a frontmatter key (blocks on schema required fields)

    echo "new body" | norn set notes/project.md --body-from-stdin --yes
        # wholesale replace body content via stdin; frontmatter kept

    norn set notes/project.md --field-json tags='["foo","bar"]' --yes
        # set a structured value via raw JSON; escape hatch

    norn set notes/project.md --field status=active --dry-run --format json
        # preview the mutation as JSON without writing

PLAN OPERATION
    
    PLAN OPERATION:
      - kind: set_frontmatter
        fields:
          path: <DOC>
          field: <KEY>
          new_value: <VALUE>

GLOBAL OPTIONS

        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
        --color <COLOR>     Color output. Honors NO_COLOR / CLICOLOR_FORCE.
        --vault <NAME>      Target the registered vault with this name (see `norn vault register`)

entries.long:
Validate vault graph facts and configured frontmatter rules

Validate vault graph facts and configured frontmatter rules.

Validation reuses graph/index facts to surface unresolved links, ambiguous links, document diagnostics, and configured frontmatter requirements. Validate does not mutate files.

USAGE
    norn validate [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS
        --format <FORMAT>
        Stdout format
        Possible values: records, jsonl, json, paths

        --summary
        Emit grouped validation finding counts instead of raw findings
        Possible values: true, false

TRIAGE FILTERS
        --code <CODE>
        Filter findings by code. Comma-separated values match any listed code

        --severity <SEVERITY>
        Filter findings by severity

        --field <FIELD>
        Filter findings by frontmatter field

        --rule <RULE>
        Filter findings by validate rule name

        --path <PATH>
        Filter findings by vault-relative path glob using config glob semantics

        --target <TARGET>
        Filter link findings by link target

        --reason <REASON>
        Filter link findings by unresolved reason

EXAMPLES
    norn validate
        # human-readable findings on the configured vault

    norn validate --format json
        # machine-readable findings for pipelines

    norn validate --severity error
        # errors only; skip warnings

    norn validate --code 'link-*'
        # broken + ambiguous links

    norn validate --code 'link-*' --format paths
        # unique source paths only; pipe-friendly

HOW VALIDATION WORKS
    Validate reads `.norn/config.yaml` for the rules that shape your vault: required frontmatter fields, allowed values, expected types, and path scoping. Each rule produces findings with a stable code and a severity (`error`, `warning`, `info`).

    Findings cover three surfaces. Frontmatter findings come from schema rules — codes like `frontmatter-required-field-missing` and `value-not-allowed`. Link findings come from graph facts — `link-target-missing`, `link-anchor-missing`, `link-block-missing`, and `link-ambiguous`. Document diagnostics come from parse — malformed frontmatter, encoding issues. Validate never writes files.

    Exit code is `1` when any finding has severity `error`, `0` otherwise. Pipelines gate on this exit code.

    Triage filters combine with AND across types and OR within a type. `--severity error --code frontmatter-required-field-missing` returns errors that match that code. `--code 'link-*'` returns the whole family. `--path 'notes/**'` scopes to a path glob; `--field`, `--rule`, `--target`, and `--reason` narrow further.

FINDING CODES
    Codes identify validation findings. Filter with --code <code>. Glob patterns supported (--code 'link-*').

    link-target-missing         A wikilink target doesn't exist in the vault.
    link-anchor-missing         The target exists but the #anchor isn't present.
    link-block-missing          The target exists but the ^block-ref isn't present.
    link-ambiguous              A wikilink resolves to multiple candidates.
    frontmatter-required-field-missing
                                A required frontmatter field is absent.
    value-not-allowed           A field's value is not in the configured set.
    field-type-invalid          A field's value doesn't match its declared type.
    frontmatter-exceeds-max-length
                                A string/list_of_strings field matches its type but exceeds max_length.
    frontmatter-forbidden-field A field that the rule forbids is present.
    document-misrouted          A doc is in a directory the rule's path selector excludes.
    frontmatter-reference-type  A field's wikilink resolves to a document whose type is outside the allowed set.

GLOBAL OPTIONS

        --no-cache-refresh  Skip the implicit cache refresh before reading the graph
